title: RAW UNREVIEWED: three-hand spelling transport must commute on unseen whole-form families
summary: RAW_UNREVIEWED_NOT_SELECTED_NOT_TESTED. If several hands realize one shared inventory through systematic allography, transformations learned on disjoint training families between hands A/B and B/C should predict the same complete C form as direct A/C transport. No semantics or historical renderer cards are inherited. Shared contexts must be established independently and hand/section confounding can make this untestable.

design.mechanism: Hand-specific finite spelling realizations of common latent forms require path-independent transformation around a three-hand triangle.
design.unit: Complete native word family in independently bounded comparable contexts; train/test split by entire family and physical leaf.
design.contrast: Commuting cross-hand transform versus independent pairwise lookup, identity, frequency matching and context-only prediction with identical model budgets.
design.prediction: Two-edge transport predicts exact unseen-family whole forms in the third hand and agrees with independently fitted direct transport; failure cannot be repaired by per-form exceptions.
design.scope: RAW proposal only; no data admission or meaning. GDT915/916 transfer baseline, quarantined legacy cross-hand renderers and IL022 cycle residual require primary review before selection. IL022 adjacency cycles are not this spelling-map triangle. Capacity not established; third hand or independently comparable contexts may be missing.
